source.quote:
14. The good effects described above in verses 2 to 13 are derived only when the lord of the house concerned is auspiciously disposed (not placed in the 6th, 8th, or 12th), is posited in his own sign or in his sign of exaltation or is

<!-- page phaladeepika/p0184 -->
retrograde. The effects will be adverse if such a planet is inauspiciously disposed, is in his inimical sign, in his sign of debilitation or is eclipsed by the Sun's rays.
source.quote_display: 14. The good effects described above in verses 2 to 13 are derived only when the lord of the house concerned is auspiciously disposed (not placed in the 6th, 8th, or 12th), is posited in his own sign or in his sign of exaltation or is retrograde. The effects will be adverse if such a planet is inauspiciously disposed, is in his inimical sign, in his sign of debilitation or is eclipsed by the Sun's rays.

extraction.verified_by: tarunrameshphotography + Claude (chapter 20 encoding, Milestone 31: INTERPRETIVE STEP TAKEN AND RECORDED -- v.14's two clauses read as auspicious = NOT dusthana AND (own OR exalted OR retrograde); adverse = dusthana OR (inimical OR debilitated OR combust), the most literal parse of 'auspiciously disposed (not placed in the 6th, 8th, or 12th), is posited in his own sign or in his sign of exaltation or is retrograde' / 'adverse if ... inauspiciously disposed, is in his inimical sign, in his sign of debilitation or is eclipsed by the Sun's rays'. A graha satisfying both clauses at once gets no verdict, mirroring `_strength`'s own retrograde+combust collision discipline rather than inventing a new tie-break)

cards.note: The shared disposition clause gating every PD.20.Strong.*/PD.20.Weak.* card. Deliberately NOT read as ch. 4's `strength` verdict: v.14 states own-sign, inimical-sign and dusthana-placement clauses that chapter 4's own strength doctrine (vv.4-5, PD.04.Strength.*) does not cover -- confirmed by reading all three PD.04.Strength.* cards in full before deciding this. Encoded as its own local criterion (a new predicate, `dasa_disposition`, Engine/facts.py::_dasa_disposition) rather than narrowing what this verse actually says to fit the existing verdict. See concept:strength-criterion-scope.
